title: Level 4 (Expert) - A-34
notes:
West's club opening lead is won by South. The contract is in danger only if diamonds are 4-0. If West has 4 diamonds, the suit can be played for 2 losers provided that the ♦K is played on the first round.

It would be a mistake to play the ♦K at trick 2, however, as South would be left with no play when East holds all 4 diamonds. South does better by crossing to the ♥A and leading a diamond toward his ♦K.

It would be wrong to cross to dummy in spades (instead of hearts). Such a play would expose the closed hand to spade forces making it difficult or impossible to pick up 4 diamonds in West's hand for 2 losers.

When the ♦K holds as West discards, South's only hope of losing just 2 diamond tricks is to endplay East in trumps. There are 2 ways this might be accomplished.

If East is 3442, South can crossruff hearts and spades and lead a club in this position. East must ruff and lead away from his ♦A.

A better chance is to play clubs immediately. If clubs are 3-3, South should play East to be 3343. There are several possible winning sequences. For example, South can continue with the ♠A and a spade ruff. 2 rounds of hearts come next, dummy ruffing. Dummy's last spade is ruffed. South exits a low trump (or anything else) and East is held to 2 trump tricks as before.

If East turns up with 4 clubs, South should play East to be 3244. Again South has more than 1 winning line. For example, South can continue with the ♠A and a spade, ruffing. South's good club is ruffed. Dummy's last spade is ruffed and the ♥K is cashed. As before, East will be endplayed into giving up 1 of his trump tricks.
